vjimc-2003-cat1-01.prompt: Let $d(k)$ denote the number of all natural divisors of a natural number $k$. Prove that for any natural number $n_0$ the sequence $\left\{d(n^2+1)\right\}_{n=n_0}^{\infty}$ is not strictly monotone.
vjimc-2003-cat1-01.answer: For even $n$, the divisors of the odd non-square $n^2+1$ pair up as $\{d,(n^2+1)/d\}$ with $d<n$ odd, so $d(n^2+1)\le n$; a strictly increasing sequence of even numbers grows by at least $2$ per step and would eventually exceed this bound, and a strictly decreasing sequence of positive integers is impossible.

vjimc-2003-cat1-02.prompt:
Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $m\times n$ real matrix with at least one non-zero element. For each $i\in\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $R_i=\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}$ be the sum of the $i$-th row of the matrix $A$, and for each $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $C_j=\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ij}$ be the sum of the $j$-th column of the matrix $A$. Prove that there exist indices $k\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ and $l\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that
$$a_{kl}>0,\quad R_k\ge 0,\quad C_l\ge 0,$$
or
$$a_{kl}<0,\quad R_k\le 0,\quad C_l\le 0.$$
vjimc-2003-cat1-02.answer: Assume not and split rows into $R_i\ge0$ / $R_i<0$ and columns into $C_j>0$ / $C_j\le0$; computing the sum of the block (negative rows)×(positive columns) in two ways shows it is both $\le0$ and $\ge0$, which forces all $R_i=C_j=0$, and then any non-zero entry works — a contradiction.

vjimc-2003-cat1-04.prompt: Let $A$ and $B$ be complex Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices having the pairs of eigenvalues $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ and $(\beta_1,\beta_2)$, respectively. Determine all possible pairs of eigenvalues $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ of the matrix $C=A+B$. (We recall that a matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ is Hermitian if and only if $a_{ij}=\overline{a_{ji}}$ for all $i$ and $j$.)
vjimc-2003-cat1-04.answer: Ordering $\alpha_1\ge\alpha_2$, $\beta_1\ge\beta_2$, $\gamma_1\ge\gamma_2$: exactly the pairs with $\gamma_1+\gamma_2=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\beta_1+\beta_2$ and $\max(\alpha_1+\beta_2,\ \alpha_2+\beta_1)\le\gamma_1\le\alpha_1+\beta_1$.
